basis: Native comparison of the sealed expected asset for csharp-B03 and csharp-B04. For every EXPECTED alternative the witness (copied unchanged from the sealed asset) is split into parts: a group A witness (match tokens) has one part per anchor token, with the anchor's sealed types and the token's span; a group B witness (match span) has one part, the witness's span with the alternative's sealed types. The tree-sitter-c-sharp tree of the witness's source, parsed by the registered native build (provenance in native; raw_native pins the local raw observation), is searched for a node of one of the part's sealed types with exactly the part's span: MATCH, else MISMATCH. A witness is MATCH when every part is, MISMATCH when one is not, and NOT_APPLICABLE when the native parse did not complete; an alternative has the result of its only witness and is executed when a completed native witness was compared. Decision D-1: a group A match says the anchor tokens are the sealed node types at those spans, not that the node holding them has any shape, and a weak match (discriminating false) proves less than a discriminating one. A discriminating group A alternative has a tier: word (a word anchor with one sealed node type), candidate (its word anchors' sealed types are candidate sets such as a keyword that may also be a modifier) or operator (no word anchor, an operator of two or more characters only); only the word tier counts as discriminating, and the counts keep the tiers, the weak matches and group B apart. Each mismatch has a disposition with a cause: GRAMMAR_DEFECT, KIND_MAP_ERROR, EXPECTED_ERROR or DESIGN_DIFFERENCE. Expectations, the kind map and the observation are not changed by this asset; a sealed value that the native result contradicts stays as sealed and is reported. The comparison covers the witnesses only: it does not say the grammar parses every construct of an alternative, and a MATCH is a property of the pinned Roslyn observation's spans on these sources. Revision r2 compares the expected asset r2 (the sealed r1 asset with its post-seal corrections: four anchor types and one alternative moved to BLOCKED) with the same raw native observation as r1, so no native run was repeated: the sealed alternatives that no correction touched are compared with their sealed values, the corrected alternatives with the corrected ones (corrected, and counted apart in corrected_match and sealed_match). r1 is the comparison of the sealed asset, with the five mismatches and their dispositions, and stays as it is.
